# Life Ledger · Deep Review 2.0.0

Life Ledger 2.0 is a redesign of the web app: Today becomes a card workspace, every page gets a new design, and the local edition opens with a complete fictional sample so anyone can see what months of use look like. The Cloudflare backend, data format and sync are unchanged.

## Today as a card workspace

- Weather (hourly curve for the selected day), mood, daily foundations, habit heatmap, focus, recent rhythm, month, photo wall, day calendar and more are cards.
- **Edit cards** adds, removes, drags, resizes and configures cards; the card library can add a second photo wall. The layout is saved.
- The quote and the mood check-in stay fixed at the top; checking a habit animates only the card you touched.

## Every page redesigned

- **Week:** review (with voice input), completed work, insights and goals as calm modules.
- **Horizon:** long-term phases side by side — one fills the page, two share it, more flow into a grid.
- **Timeline:** daily, weekly and monthly reading, a photo view and a calendar view; any day opens for editing.
- **Review:** one month at a time with completion per habit, weekly rhythm, focus time and a written reflection (monthly review lives only here).
- **Habit settings:** targets, colors, icons and daily/weekly/monthly frequency, with motion restored.
- One design family (documented in `docs/DESIGN.md`), Apple system fonts by default, appearance and font moved into Settings.

## Local edition with a three-month sample

- The local-only web app (GitHub Pages) opens with three months of fictional sample life: habits, mood, daily notes, weekly and monthly reviews, long-term plans and bundled illustrative photos.
- **Settings → Clear local data** starts blank; **Load sample data** brings the sample back.
- Earlier local records are kept: since 2.0.1 every visitor sees the sample, and records made before are stored as a backup in that browser — **Settings → Restore earlier records** brings them back.
- The sample follows the interface language (English, Simplified Chinese, German) and keeps anything you edited yourself.

## Language and accessibility

- Switching language now updates every page, dialog, menu option, accessibility label and the sample data immediately, on desktop and mobile.

## Cloud edition

- Same Cloudflare Access protection, D1 synchronization, private photos and read-only Google Calendar; no database migration.
- The sample data and the local clearing controls never run in the cloud edition.

## Roll back to 1.3

Version 1.3.0 stays available at tag `v1.3.0`.

- **Local edition (GitHub Pages):** run the *Publish local-only PWA* workflow from tag `v1.3.0` (Actions → Publish local-only PWA → Run workflow → `v1.3.0`), or check out `v1.3.0` and push it to the branch Pages publishes from.
- **Self-hosted Cloudflare:** check out `v1.3.0` and deploy it the same way you deployed 2.0 (Cloudflare Pages also keeps every previous deployment, which can be restored from the dashboard). Your D1 data is not changed by either version.
- Browser data stays in the browser; switching versions does not delete it.

The previous stable source remains available at tag `v1.3.0`.
